Unfortunately, Utah couldn’t avoid putting the Timberwolves on the line (27-of-32) and weren’t consistently able to knock down shots (42.5 percent from the field and 29.2 percent from deep) in a 115-100 loss.
Minnesota only shot 41 percent from the field during the opening quarter, with most of the damage done in the paint (16 points).
Meanwhile, Utah’s scoring was a balanced distribution both in terms of shot location (three 3-pointers and 10 points in the paint) and responsibility (five Jazzmen scored five points in the frame).
Minnesota got 16 points off the bench, which helped push the home team to a slight 28-25 lead after 12 minutes.
As a result, the Timberwolves opened their first double-digit lead of the game, which reached 10 near the midway point of the frame.

Keyonte George (11 points, seven assists) and Darryn Peterson (12 points, three assists) joined forces to keep Utah within striking distance, but Minnesota still took a 57-51 advantage into the halftime break.
